Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking the bridge yesterday. To recap for our execs: Boldt saw a significant increase in inference latency and 5xx errors across the checkout flow between 15:14–15:42 PT on May 1, which materially impacted conversion for ~30 minutes. We need a written RCA and clear runbook updates so our ops team can trust the integration moving forward.

Can you provide: 1) a short RCA with root cause, 2) the mitigations you plan to ship and owners + dates, and 3) confirmation of any SLA credit mechanics. I've attached our timeline export (boldt_incident_timeline.csv) and included Keisha on copy.

We appreciate a doc we can share with our CTO today.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-incident RCA and next steps re: slowdown on May 1

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. Attaching a preliminary RCA (see boldt_prelim_rca.pdf) and an initial action tracker. High level: we observed a sudden shift in request length distribution and a pathological KV-cache evictions pattern on the dedicated pool serving your model variant; that caused increased tail latency and a cascade of retries that surfaced as elevated 5xx rates.

Immediate actions we took during the incident:
- scoped traffic to the baseline model variant and ramped fallback to smaller-quantized variant (temporary mitigation)
- increased autoscaling headroom for the affected pool by 25%
- disabled one experimental scheduling kernel path that amplified cache churn

Planned corrective actions with owners and ETA (full tracker attached):
- Jonas Weber: kernel rollback + canary patch (PR #8421) — ETA 2027-05-04
- Marissa Cole: expanded end-to-end perf tests & regression alerts on sample sets — ETA 2027-05-07
- Kimberly Park: confirm mutual action plan & customer comms; coordinate SLA credit discussion — ETA 2027-05-06

We will update the doc and post a final RCA once the patch is validated. For transparency I created SUP-1234 to track the work; link in the doc.

Vivek
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: boldt_prelim_rca.pdf (PDF stub), boldt_action_tracker.xlsx (XLSX stub)

Subject: Technical RCA write-up + remediation checklist (SUP-1234)

Team / Alex — attaching the technical supplement in the shared doc (link below) and summarizing the root cause and the specific changes we will make. Key findings:
1) KV cache eviction storm: an unlucky alignment of long-context requests and a minor change in our kernel prefetch heuristics led to frequent cache churn; the miss penalty for the affected working set is high because of remote memory access patterns.
2) Autoscaler threshold tuning: our default margin for dedicated pools assumed a narrower length distribution and aggressively downsized the pool under transient load.
3) Retry amplification: client-side retry backoffs were configured conservatively and amplified the transient server-side resource pressure.

Remediations (owner / acceptance criteria / ETA):
- Kernel rollback & disable experimental prefetch path (Jonas) / verified in canary (p95 latency within baseline) / 2027-05-04 (rolled)
- Autoscaler parameter change: increase headroom and add cooldown window (SRE runbook updated) / Marissa to validate via synthetic burst tests / 2027-05-10
- Client retry guidance: publish recommended retry/backoff settings for Boldt SDK + opt-in configuration to respect server congestion header / Marissa / 2027-05-07
- Observability: add a dedicated alert for cache eviction rate and request-length histogram drift / Jonas / 2027-05-05

I opened PRs: #8421 (kernel rollback), #8437 (eviction alert), #8450 (autoscaler tuning). Links in SUP-1234. Once the canary has 48 hours of stable metrics we'll schedule a controlled rollout.

Jonas Weber
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
